title: Migration builds a metropolis
hook: What happened after migrants arrived in Chicago?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: A migration map should not stop at an arrival dot.

claims.text: 1905: A newspaper. The Chicago Defender begins publication.
claims.source: https://home.nps.gov/articles/chicago-s-black-metropolis-understanding-history-through-a-historic-place-teaching-with-historic-places.htm — Reading on Black Metropolis: Defender, 1910–1920 migration, 1920s construction, Depression

claims.text: 1910–20: Northward movement. African Americans leave the South for Chicago.
claims.source: https://home.nps.gov/articles/chicago-s-black-metropolis-understanding-history-through-a-historic-place-teaching-with-historic-places.htm — Reading on Black Metropolis: Defender, 1910–1920 migration, 1920s construction, Depression

claims.text: 1920s: Building institutions. Black-owned projects develop on the South Side.
claims.source: https://home.nps.gov/articles/chicago-s-black-metropolis-understanding-history-through-a-historic-place-teaching-with-historic-places.htm — Reading on Black Metropolis: Defender, 1910–1920 migration, 1920s construction, Depression

claims.text: 1929: Economic shock. The Depression damages Black Metropolis businesses.
claims.source: https://home.nps.gov/articles/chicago-s-black-metropolis-understanding-history-through-a-historic-place-teaching-with-historic-places.htm — Reading on Black Metropolis: Defender, 1910–1920 migration, 1920s construction, Depression

claims.text: A migration map should not stop at an arrival dot. The Chicago Defender encouraged northward migration, and Chicago’s Black community built businesses, banks and cultural institutions amid exclusion. Later economic shocks weakened that base. Movement and institution building belong to the same story.
claims.source: https://home.nps.gov/articles/chicago-s-black-metropolis-understanding-history-through-a-historic-place-teaching-with-historic-places.htm — Reading on Black Metropolis: Defender, 1910–1920 migration, 1920s construction, Depression

claims.text: The South dot is a regional anchor; this is not every migrant’s route.
